title: Grieving father puzzled by son's deadly fight
article: A portrait is now emerging of the two friends at the centre of a violent incident that led to both being killed, one by police gunfire.

Police say they responded to a call about a fight at a Portage Avenue apartment block Dec. 30 to find two men, one armed with a knife, in an altercation. Zunga Bashir, 24, was fatally shot by officers trying to intervene in the fight.
James David Ibrahim, 28, was also killed; police believe he Bashir stabbed him before he was shot by police.

Ramadan Bashir, father of the man killed by police, says his son and Ibrahim were best friends and roommates. The last time he saw them, about a week before their deaths, they came to visit him together.
Bashir is at a loss to explain why his son would hurt his friend.
"He was very quiet. He played soccer. He was a very nice boy," he told CBC News. "We don't know, actually, what has happened which led him to stab his friend and roommate."
Bashir says police have told him alcohol was involved in the fight between his son and his friend, but he has heard conflicting stories about why police shot the young man.

"They are the peacekeepers. They're not supposed to just shoot people," he said of police. "When they arrived and they found one person is dead and another has a knife, at least they should do the possible thing to arrest him alive."
Police have been tight-lipped about exactly what took place before Bashir was shot. A police officer remains on administrative leave, as is procedure after a police shooting.

Including Bashir, Winnipeg Police killed three people during 2005. Howard Fleury, 34, was shot by police responding to a domestic complaint in early December. Matthew Dumas, 18, was shot during a scuffle with police in late January.
